title: Many-body topology in parity-preserving tensor networks
authors: Maksimilian Usoltcev, Nguyen Hanh Dung, Carolin Wille, Matteo Rizzi, Alexander Altland
abstract: Planar parity-preserving tensor networks (ppTNs) admit a fermionic formulation in which the Gaussian, efficiently contractible limit is deformed by local interactions. We investigate how many-body methods can be used to analyze such contractions in a minimal two-parameter ppTN. Its contraction is simultaneously an interacting fermionic partition function, a loop gas, a deformed toric-code norm, and a quartic Ising model, allowing the same phase diagram to be approached with complementary tools. At its center lies a `topological island', characterized beyond the Gaussian limit by a boundary-twist $\mathbb Z_2$ indicator that reduces to Chern-number parity and admits a loop-winding interpretation under duality. Fermionic perturbation theory predicts the interacting phase boundaries, tensor-network numerics establish their critical behavior, and the loop and spin descriptions reveal a self-dual line with a $c=1$ four-state-Potts multicritical fixed point.
summary: This work investigates the many-body topology embedded in planar parity-preserving tensor networks by showing its equivalence to several distinct physical models, including the Ising model and loop gas. By unifying these descriptions, the authors map out a comprehensive phase diagram centered around a robust 'topological island' phase. The study demonstrates the power of using complementary theoretical tools to characterize complex quantum critical behavior.
main_problem: The paper analyzes the many-body topology encoded within planar parity-preserving tensor networks (ppTNs) and unifies its description across multiple seemingly different physical models.
main_result: The phase diagram is shown to be unified by complementary descriptions (fermionic, loop gas, Ising model), revealing a central 'topological island' phase characterized by a robust $\mathbb{Z}_2$ invariant.
method: The analysis employs fermionic perturbation theory, tensor-network numerics, and duality transformations to map the system's partition function onto several equivalent mathematical and physical forms.
model_or_system: The core model is a two-parameter planar parity-preserving tensor network (ppTN) defined by parameters $a$ and $b$. This model is shown to be equivalent to a loop gas, a deformed toric-code state, and a quartic Ising model.
key_observables: The topological invariant ($\sigma_{\text{topo}}$), the Chern number ($C$), and the phase boundaries separating different ordered phases.
important_parameters: The two control parameters, $a$ and $b$, which govern the deformation away from the free-fermion limit. The special line $b = 1 - a^2$ is also crucial.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on mapping the interacting system to an effective free-fermion theory to predict phase boundaries, and the cancellation of fixed seam factors confirms the topological invariant's robustness.
figures_summary: Figure 1 provides an overview of the common phase diagram, illustrating the 'topological island' across the loop gas, deformed toric code, quartic Ising, and fermionic representations.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the equivalence between the ppTN and several other models, analyzes the topological invariant using fermionic methods, and uses numerical and analytical techniques to map out the complete phase diagram and critical lines.
why_interesting: The deep connection between topological order, critical phenomena (Ising model), and modern computational tools (tensor networks) provides a powerful framework for understanding quantum phase transitions in strongly correlated systems.
